title: Faster release verification
scope: The stable launcher verifies every release file on each command. One iterative directory walk now checks the inventory and contents, and every expected file still gets a complete content hash. Measured in process with a warm cache on the same immutable bundle: this is the verifier component, not a whole command.

title: Shorter launch for one-call plans
scope: Ringo no longer imports the thread pool, and the logging and traceback modules it pulls in, at start-up; plans that make a single call never use it. Fresh-process commands with simulated backends, both arms selected through equal private fixture approvals, no provider calls. Local machine overhead, not live-provider latency.

title: Lean Codex calls
scope: Ringo's Codex calls are single tool-free turns, yet each carried the Codex agent prompt, the code-mode and multi-agent tool schemas, and skills, permission and environment blocks. The codex-chatgpt preset now replaces the agent prompt with one line and drops those blocks; Ringo's own prompt is unchanged byte for byte. Same model and reasoning effort on both sides, native ChatGPT login. Spot check: the lean writer's answer scored the same as before on the pilot's own checker; one sample does not establish equal quality, and whole benchmark runs were not repeated.

title: Calls end when the backend exits
scope: Ringo used to notice that a backend process had exited only at Popen's next poll, whose sleeps grow to fifty milliseconds. A blocking wait in a helper thread now wakes the call at once, within the new soft time limits. Fresh-process commands with simulated backends against the release active at the time, equal private fixture approvals, no provider calls. Local machine overhead, not live-provider latency.
